newsitem.title: USA: Treasury's Rubin sees no U.S. recession on horizon.
newsitem.headline: Treasury's Rubin sees no U.S. recession on horizon.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Tuesday said the Clinton administration does not see a recession on the horizon anytime in the near future.

"We don't see a recession as far out as we can reasonably look to see right now," Rubin said when questioned about the administration's economic assumptions during testimony before the tax-writing House Ways and Means Committee.
Rubin also expressed concern about slow economic growth in Japan and a high level of unemployment in Germany.
He said the United States was concerned that Japan has had a low rate of growth for four or five years and that conditions were uncertain.
"We do feel that it is very important that Japan focus on domestic demand and growth," Rubin said. He also noted that Germany recently reported the highest level of unemployment in decades.
"Clearly there are a lot of issues that need to be addressed in other countries of the (Group of Seven) if they are going to have robust economies, and that is important to us," Rubin said.
